title: Covariant derived replacement formulas and base-change
statement:
Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, left fibrations, simplicial categories, model localizations and enriched diagrams as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation], [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] and [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification]. Let $B$ be a small quasicategory, $A=\mathfrak C[B]$, and let $U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}$ be the ordinary covariant unstraightening right Quillen functor from the projective model category of enriched $A$-diagrams to the covariant slice over $B$. Write $L_B$ for its ordinary left adjoint, so $L_B\dashv U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}$. The derived unit and counit of this Quillen adjunction are represented by the replacement formulas
$$X\longrightarrow U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}T L_BQX,\qquad L_BQ U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}TF\longrightarrow F,$$
with $Q$ a cofibrant and $T$ a fibrant replacement, and are equivalences in the localized infinity categories; these displayed arrows are localized maps, with the replacement weak equivalences inverted, rather than asserted strict maps to an unreplaced object. For an objectwise Kan enriched diagram $F$, a trivial-fibration cofibrant replacement remains fibrant and does not change its localized unstraightening or enriched evaluation. Under a pullback $f:B'\to B$, the displayed replacement transformations and the enriched-evaluation comparison commute coherently with derived restriction in the localized categories, using the actual base-change isomorphism of $U^{\mathrm{cov}}$; hence the normalized derived equivalence is natural under pullback and precomposition.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.1.2 (covariant dual), Proposition 4.2.4.4 and Section 3.3.2; replacement formulas and base-change compatibility in the ordinary covariant model presentation

proof.text: Put $\mathcal M_B=\mathsf{sSet}_{/B}^{\mathrm{cov}}$ and $\mathcal D_B=\operatorname{Fun}_{\Delta}(\mathfrak C[B],\mathsf{sSet})_{\mathrm{proj}}$. By [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation], all objects of $\mathcal M_B$ are cofibrant, the fibrant objects are left fibrations, the fibrant diagrams are objectwise Kan, and the ordinary adjunction $L_B\dashv U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}$ is a Quillen equivalence. Choose functorial cofibrant replacements $q:Q\to1$ by trivial fibrations and fibrant replacements $t:1\to T$ by trivial cofibrations in the respective model categories. Write $\ell_B=\mathbf LL_B$ and $R_B=\mathbf RU_B^{\mathrm{cov}}$. The derived adjunction of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] gives $\ell_B(X)=L_BQX$ and $R_B(F)=U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}TF$ after localization, and gives its coherent unit and counit by inserting $q,t$ into the ordinary unit and counit. No simplicial structure on the ordinary adjunction or on the replacements is needed.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction: agent-expanded covariant replacement and base-restriction foundation

proof.text: At $X$, the unit is the localized composite $X\xleftarrow{q_X}QX\xrightarrow{\eta_{QX}}U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}L_BQX\xrightarrow{U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}t_{L_BQX}}U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}TL_BQX$, with the first arrow inverted, by [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. The adjoint of its last two arrows is $t_{L_BQX}:L_BQX\to TL_BQX$. Its source is the image under $L_B$ of a cofibrant object, its target is fibrant, and this map is a weak equivalence. The Quillen-equivalence criterion in [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] therefore makes $QX\to U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}TL_BQX$ a weak equivalence. Inverting $q_X$ proves the asserted unit formula and its equivalence.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction: agent-expanded covariant replacement and base-restriction foundation

proof.text: At $F$, use the localized composite $L_BQ U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}TF\xrightarrow{L_Bq_{U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}TF}}L_BU_B^{\mathrm{cov}}TF\xrightarrow{\epsilon_{TF}}TF\xleftarrow{t_F}F$, inverting the last arrow, as prescribed by [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. The adjoint of the composite to $TF$ is exactly $q_{U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}TF}:Q U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}TF\to U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}TF$. This is a weak equivalence with cofibrant source, and $TF$ is fibrant, so [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] makes the composite to $TF$ a weak equivalence. Thus the counit has the asserted localized formula and is an equivalence. The unit and counit are coherent transformations by the derived-adjunction theorem. The pointwise criterion [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] makes them equivalences in the entire functor categories, so $\ell_B$ and $R_B$ are inverse equivalences.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction: agent-expanded covariant replacement and base-restriction foundation

proof.text: If $F$ is objectwise Kan and $a:QF\to F$ is a projective trivial-fibration cofibrant replacement, then $QF\to *$ is the composite of the fibration $a$ and the fibration $F\to *$. Hence $QF$ is fibrant as well as cofibrant; no claim that restriction preserves projective cofibrancy is used. By [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation], $U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}a$ is an equivalence of left fibrations. For enriched evaluation, [lem-coef-kan-diagram-localized-evaluation] supplies $e_B(F)=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(F)\eta_B$ and the localized equivalence $E_B$; it explicitly says that the transformation $e_B(a):e_B(QF)\to e_B(F)$ is an equivalence of entire coherent diagrams. Its restriction to bifibrant diagrams is precisely the enriched-evaluation comparison specified in the item. Thus both unstraightening and enriched evaluation are unchanged after localization.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction: agent-expanded covariant replacement and base-restriction foundation

proof.text: For $f:B'\to B$ let $r_fF=F\mathfrak C[f]$ and let $p_f$ be pullback of left fibrations. Restriction preserves Kan values and objectwise weak equivalences. A horn lifting problem for a pullback left fibration projects to the same problem before pullback, so [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] proves that $p_f$ preserves left fibrations. The fiber over $b'$ is the old fiber over $f(b')$, so the fiberwise weak-equivalence criterion of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] proves preservation of weak equivalences between fibrant objects. The fibrant-subcategory localization and full functor-category universal property of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] therefore define $p_f,r_f$ on localizations. On fibrant diagrams the actual base-change isomorphism in the presentation node is $p_fU_B^{\mathrm{cov}}\cong U_{B'}^{\mathrm{cov}}r_f$, compatible with composites of base maps. Localize it to obtain $\beta_f:p_fR_B\simeq R_{B'}r_f$. This is derived restriction, calculated on fibrant representatives.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction: agent-expanded covariant replacement and base-restriction foundation

proof.text:
Suppress the base subscript on the derived adjunction $\ell\dashv R$ and use primes over $B'$. Define the comparison of left adjoints by the actual composite of coherent transformations
$$\alpha_f:\ell'p_f\xrightarrow{\ell'p_f\eta}\ell'p_fR\ell\xrightarrow{\ell'\beta_f\ell}\ell'R'r_f\ell\xrightarrow{\epsilon'r_f\ell}r_f\ell.$$
Every factor is an equivalence by step 3 and step 5. Its compatibility with the units is the explicit identity
$$R'\alpha_f\circ\eta'p_f=\beta_f\ell\circ p_f\eta.$$
Indeed move $\eta'$ past $\ell'(\beta_f\ell\circ p_f\eta)$ by naturality, then cancel $R'\epsilon'\circ\eta'R'=1$. These are the unit naturality and right triangle of the coherent derived adjunction supplied by [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. Thus this comparison makes the derived unit commute with restriction; the formula identifies which comparison is meant, rather than choosing an arbitrary equivalence.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction: agent-expanded covariant replacement and base-restriction foundation

proof.text:
The same explicit comparison gives the counit identity
$$r_f\epsilon\circ\alpha_fR=\epsilon'r_f\circ\ell'\beta_f.$$
To verify it, expand $\alpha_fR$. First move $r_f\epsilon$ past $\epsilon'$ by counit naturality; move it past $\beta_f$ by naturality of $\beta_f$; the remaining adjacent factors are $p_fR\epsilon\circ p_f\eta R=1$, the unprimed right derived triangle. Here all composites are in the localized functor categories of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], so these are coherent homotopies, not equations of unreplaced model objects. This proves compatibility of the particular replacement counit in step 3, because that step identifies it with the actual derived counit.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction: agent-expanded covariant replacement and base-restriction foundation

proof.text:
These comparisons have the base coherences as well. For $g:B''\to B'$ the comparison $\beta_{fg}$ is the composite $(\beta_g r_f)\circ(p_g\beta_f)$, using the composition compatibility of actual unstraightening base change in [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. Expanding step 6 twice and cancelling the middle derived unit/counit triangle gives
$$\alpha_{fg}=(r_g\alpha_f)\circ(\alpha_g p_f),$$
with the canonical identifications of iterated restrictions; for the identity base map it gives the identity comparison. The coherent adjunction of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] performs the same whiskerings and triangle homotopies on transformations and their higher simplices. The full functor-category localization property of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] carries the original base-change composition data to this data coherently: restriction to fibrant representatives is an equivalence of full functor categories, so the spaces of lifts of those specified diagrams and coherences are contractible. This establishes simultaneous coherence, without asserting that $f^*Q=Qf^*$ or $f^*T=Tf^*$ as strict replacement functors.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction: agent-expanded covariant replacement and base-restriction foundation

proof.text:
Finally [lem-coef-kan-diagram-evaluation-restriction] gives $E_{B'}r_f\simeq f^*E_B$ with joint identity, composition, transformation and higher-simplex coherence. Its replacement clause explicitly compares $Q_{B'}(r_fF)\to r_fF$, even when $r_f(Q_BF)$ is not cofibrant. Via the fibrant-subcategory localization equivalences of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], these $E_B$ are the enriched-evaluation comparisons used above. Normalize the straightening equivalence as $\operatorname{St}_B=E_B\ell_B$. Compose $E_{B'}\alpha_f$ with the displayed comparison to obtain
$$\operatorname{St}_{B'}p_f\simeq E_{B'}r_f\ell_B\simeq f^*\operatorname{St}_B.$$
Step 8 and the cited evaluation-restriction coherence give all base coherences of this composite, while steps 6 and 7 give its compatibility with the replacement unit and counit. This is the required normalized equivalence, natural under pullback and precomposition.
